---
title: Run it yourself
description: "Install, add a free Reown project id, and run the whole app on your machine against mainnet."
icon: Terminal
---

<Steps>
<Step>

### Install

Node 24 or newer and pnpm 11.

```bash
pnpm install
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Configure

Copy `apps/web/.env.example` to `apps/web/.env.local`, fill in the first two rows, and add the relayer variables yourself if you want gasless:

| Variable | Needed for |
|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_REOWN_PROJECT_ID` | EVM and Solana wallets (free at dashboard.reown.com; add `http://localhost:3030` to its domains) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_DOCS_URL` | optional; default to hashi.cash and docs.hashi.cash |
| `RELAYER_PRIVATE_KEY`, `BASE_RPC_URL` | optional, server-only: the gasless relayer |
| `ARRIVAL_SWEEP_TOKEN`, `ARRIVAL_STORE_DIR` | optional, server-only: the swap contracts' keeper. Without it (and a sweep run), swaps into PUSD or MUSD fall back to two approvals |

</Step>
<Step>

### Run

```bash
pnpm dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3030/swap`. Quotes are live from mainnet straight away; real swaps use real money in your own wallets.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Checks

```bash
pnpm lint
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
```

The tests cover addresses and recipient guards, the THORChain memo and Bitcoin Cash deposit rules, Cauldron's fees, route costs and ranking, the relayer's policy, the swap state and the tracker's steps, the swap contract in the Bitcoin Cash VM, the automatic trade and its keeper, Electrum failover and the tracker's live progress.
